newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends down, gilts up, auction discounted.
newsitem.headline: India call ends down, gilts up, auction discounted.

text.p: Indian call money eased on good funds supply to end Thursday at 1.0-1.25 percent against opening quotes of 2.0-2.5 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was between 1.5 percent and 2.0 percent.

"There is little chance of rates moving up," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Rates are largely sentiment-driven and right now, it (sentiment) is soft. Sentiment will be affected only if liquidity is sucked out in a major way."
"Even the announcement of a fresh government bond issue may not have much impact as the market seems to have discounted it," he added.
Dealers said prices of government securities ended up in active trade.
"Some players are still cautious but by and large the market seems to have factored in the likelihood of a new bond issue," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
Market players have been speculating that the government will announce a bond issue to take advantage of the easy liquidity and mop up excess funds with banks.
"But with each passing day and no announcement (of a bond issue) from the government, the market is discounting and getting on with business," said a dealer.
After the market closed, the government announced a six-year 30 billion bond auction on July 16.
Dealers said trade on Thursday was concentrated in securities with maturities up to the medium-term.
"There is also some interest in long bonds, but most of the action is in short- to medium-term stocks," said a dealer. "There was good demand for the 12.14 percent 2000 stock."

The 12.14 percent 2000 stock trade on Thursday at 102.27 rupees against its last traded 102.19, the 12 percent 1999 rose to 103.05 from 102.93 while the 12.59 percent 2004 traded between 101.22 and 101.42 against 101.40, dealers said.
The 13.80 percent 2002 traded at 106.65 and and 106.70 against 106.68, dealers said. The 13.05 percent 2007 traded at 103.40 and 103.43.
